subject.title: fix(agents): stop stable tool argument churn

question: Should generic same-tool, stable-result argument churn be a global hard-veto condition at the configured circuit-breaker threshold, including for existing repetitive multi-argument workflows?
rationale: The proposed classifier intentionally broadens a safety boundary from exact repeated arguments to a semantic heuristic; tests cannot determine the acceptable false-positive trade-off or whether user-supplied thresholds must govern it.

options.title: Adopt the heuristic with the configuration contract
options.body: Honor configured loop-detection thresholds, add boundary tests for the linked scenario and benign repeated work, and retain the heuristic as the global hard-veto policy.

options.title: Keep exact-argument global vetoes
options.body: Do not broaden the global circuit breaker until a more specific signal can distinguish harmful churn from legitimate cyclic tool work.

recommendation.title: Adopt the heuristic with the configuration contract
recommendation.body: Honor configured loop-detection thresholds, add boundary tests for the linked scenario and benign repeated work, and retain the heuristic as the global hard-veto policy.
